newsitem.title: USA: West U.S. spot power higher after nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: West U.S. spot power higher after nuke outage.

text.p: U.S. spot power prices in the western U.S. were supported by news of the early-morning shutdown of a key nuclear unit in California, but they ended the day mixed following Monday's run-up, market sources said.
"Without Edison (Edison International's Southern California Edison Co.) buying, we would have seen softer prices," said a California trader.
Edison said today their 1,080-megawatt unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant near San Clemente, Calif., was taken off-line for repairs to a leak in the reactor's coolant system.
No estimate was given for how long the unit would be down, but market sources said it did not seem to be a major outage.

San Onofre's 1,070-MW unit 2 is due to shut Nov 30 for scheduled refueling, and continues to be monitored for possible problems with water seals which may require it to be taken off-line for repairs ahead of the refuel.

Elsewhere in the region, some coal plants in the Northwest which were down for unplanned work since late last week were back up. PacifiCorp said Tuesday a 670-MW unit at its Centralia plant in Washington state was restarted late Monday.
Confirmation was not available on the status of Montana Power's 700-MW Colstrip unit 4, which was due to restart early Tuesday.
Next-day California-Oregon border (COB) prices were last quoted $17.00-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $16.50-18.00 on Monday.
Palo Verde prices for Tuesday were quoted at $20.00-22.00, compared with deals between $19.00 and $26.00 on Monday, traders said.
COB for October was last quoted $16.00-16.25 per MWh, up from $15.55-15.80 on Friday. October Palo Verde was quoted $16.25-16.40, up from $16.00-16.25 on Friday.
Mid-Columbia for October was last quoted $15.65-15.85.
